newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SAS says to unveil five carrier alliance in May.
newsitem.headline: SAS says to unveil five carrier alliance in May.

text.p: Scandinavian airline SAS said on Thursday it would unveil details of an alliance with four other international carriers next month.

It is almost a year since SAS and Germany's Lufthansa joined forces and now the Scandinavian carrier is embarking on the next stage -- a cooperation with United Airlines, Thai International, and Air Canada.
"We will release details in Frankfurt on May 14," SAS spokesman Peter Forssman told Reuters.
"The idea is not for a merger of the five airlines but it is based on commercial agreements where bonus programmes, streamlining and seamless service are part of the cooperation."

In February this year SAS declined to comment on market talks that it was to participate in a new nine-airline global airline, designed to counter the partnership between British Airways and American Airlines.

The new club was to be headed by United Airlines Inc and Lufthansa and include Air Canada, SAS, Thai Airways International, Brazil's Varig, All-Nippon Airways, South African Airways and British Midland.
Forssman said SAS had been in working groups with four of those airlines since last October in a bid to form some kind of closer cooperation, but not with any others.
"But in the long-term future the doors are not closed for enlargement of the alliance," he said.
Forssman said from the start of talks last October, the five airlines had hoped to reach some kind of agreement ahead of the summer of 1997.
"Now we have come to the point where we are ready to release our work," he said.
"But it is fair to say that this is a process and all things will not be in place on day one."
The alliance between the five carriers will involve over 180,000 employees and almost 1,300 planes.
The biggest player in the team will be United Airlines that has about 570 planes and 86,000 staff.
Second comes Lufthansa and Air Canada with about 220 planes and 25,000 staff.
SAS has 161 planes and 25,000 staff while Thai has 73 planes and 22,000 staff.
